note: 'He was a hairy man,” they answered, “with a leather belt around his waist.” “It was Elijah the Tishbite,” said the king.' (2Kgs 1:8). The description and the name are one verse.
The belt is named in both.
'John wore a garment of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist' (Matt 3:4).
'He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire' (Matt 3:12), two verses after the tree.
'every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down' (Matt 3:10).

Matt 3:10 has the unfruitful tree and Matt 3:12 the chaff burned, in that order -- the order Psalm 1 gives them. John does not name the psalm, so the join is the graph's; the pair and its sequence are his.
'You snakes! You brood of vipers!' (Matt 23:33). Both in one address, neither explaining the other -- which is the whole of what the corpus does to connect them.
'But Jesus answered, It is written: Man shall not live on bread alone' (Matt 4:4). He names it as scripture in the answering.
'Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples' (Matt 23:1) opens the discourse; v33 is inside it and does not name the speaker. The attribution runs from the top of the chapter.

'And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.' (Matt 11:14), and again at Matt 17:12, 'Elijah is come already'. Said outright rather than left to the clothing, and Mal 4:5 -- 'I will send you Elijah the prophet' -- is what it answers.
The bread is named in both.
'like chaff driven off by the wind' (Ps 1:4).

'Not so the wicked!' (Ps 1:4) -- the phrase turns on the verse before it, so the two pictures are one sentence apart and the second is defined against the first. Implied because neither verse names the other picture: v3 has the tree and v4 has the chaff, and what joins them is the word 'not' at the head of v4.
'You brood of vipers' (Matt 23:33), the address John uses at Matt 3:7.
v33 says only 'You'. The addressees are named at Matt 23:2, 'The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat', and the discourse does not change audience. John uses the same words of them at Matt 3:7.
